title: Quantifying emotional arousal through pupillary response: a novel approach for isolating the luminosity effect and predicting affective states
title_zh: 通过瞳孔反应量化情绪唤醒：隔离光度效应并预测情感状态的新方法
abstract: Abstract Background Pupil dilation is widely used as a physiological marker associated with emotional arousal, but confounding factors such as stimulus luminosity and surrounding environmental light have greatly limited its practical usefulness. This study presents a new approach to model and quantify the effect of luminosity on pupil dilation. Materials and methods We validated this approach by showing 32 video clips with different content and emotional intensity to 45 participants, who reported their level of emotional arousal after each video. We developed a model capable of predicting the effect of luminosity on pupil size as a function of screen brightness, which adapts to individual physiological differences and different types of monitors through a brief pre-experimental calibration. We therefore estimated the pupil-size component predicted from screen luminosity and subtracted it from the total recorded pupil signal, obtaining a luminosity-corrected, arousal-sensitive residual. From this residual, we predicted each participant’s self-reported arousal for each video using two models. We first used a simple linear regression model and then an Extreme Gradient Boosting model. Results With the linear regression model, when we used the luminosity-corrected pupil size, we obtained a correlation between predicted and self-reported arousal of $$r$$ = 0.65 ± 0.12, and $$R2$$ of 0.43 ± 0.12. The uncorrected pupil size, instead, showed virtually no predictive power ( $$r$$ = 0.26 ± 0.15, $$R2$$ = 0.09 ± 0.089). When we used the Extreme Gradient Boosting model, we obtained even better results in the case of luminosity correction ( $$r$$ = 0.765 ± 0.047, $$R2$$ = 0.556 ± 0.085). Conclusions Our results highlight that modelling and attenuating luminosity-driven pupil variation is crucial for improving the prediction of self-reported arousal from pupillary responses.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景：瞳孔扩张被广泛用作与情绪唤醒相关的生理标记，但刺激光度和周围环境光等混杂因素极大地限制了其实际应用。本研究提出了一种新方法，用于建模和量化光度对瞳孔扩张的影响。材料与方法：我们通过向45名参与者展示32段不同内容和情绪强度的视频剪辑，并让他们在每段视频后报告情绪唤醒水平，验证了该方法。我们开发了一种模型，能够根据屏幕亮度预测光度对瞳孔尺寸的影响，并通过简短的预实验校准适应个体生理差异和不同类型的显示器。随后，我们估计了由屏幕光度预测的瞳孔尺寸成分，并将其从总记录的瞳孔信号中减去，得到光度校正后的、对唤醒敏感的残差。基于该残差，我们使用两种模型预测每位参与者对每段视频的自我报告唤醒水平。首先使用简单线性回归模型，然后使用极端梯度提升（XGBoost）模型。结果：使用线性回归模型时，采用光度校正后的瞳孔尺寸，预测值与自我报告唤醒的相关系数为 r = 0.65 ± 0.12，R² = 0.43 ± 0.12；未校正的瞳孔尺寸几乎没有预测能力（r = 0.26 ± 0.15，R² = 0.09 ± 0.089）。使用极端梯度提升模型时，在光度校正的情况下获得了更好的结果（r = 0.765 ± 0.047，R² = 0.556 ± 0.085）。结论：我们的结果强调，建模并抑制光度驱动的瞳孔变化对于提高从瞳孔反应预测自我报告唤醒至关重要。
